title: Bittensor Daily News — November 6, 2026
summary: SN92 REAX reaches the top tied rank on the independent Decision Index; SN64 Chutes lists Qwen3.8 open weights. SN99’s Thirty Spokes registration is replaced, with its successor still unnamed. Plus wallet activation facts, SN121’s sealed-reference challenge, miner tooling and Shizzy’s Leadpoet replay and Carbon schedule.

ecosystem.headline: OpenTensor explains post-quantum wallets; the shared activation gate remains off
ecosystem.summary: On November 6, the OpenTensor Foundation explained ML-DSA-65/Falcon signature options and optional key rotation. It says standard post-quantum accounts need no registration deposit, while rotating accounts permanently reserve 0.2 TAO; existing wallets remain supported. This explains code already covered in releases 487/488. It does not establish enabled mainnet signing: HashedAccountsEnabled was still false at finalized runtime 488 block 9,447,649, timestamp 14:31:24 UTC November 6. The reviewed implementation checks that shared gate for fixed and rotating post-quantum authorization. No wallet creation, fund movement or cryptographic audit was performed.

updates.headline: SN17 404—GEN merges opt-in concurrent native proof contexts
updates.summary: November 5 PR82 merges opt-in support for one to eight independent native prover contexts. They grow lazily as calls queue; the default remains one. The team reports local artifact tests; a published release and installation by miners were not verified.

updates.headline: SN28 SayGM merges registry-selected Phala KMS safeguards for new workers
updates.summary: A November 6 gm-miner merge makes new confidential-worker creation select a non-expiring Phala key management (KMS) contract allowed by the registry, using its default or an explicit permitted override. Without an allowed explicit override, missing or invalid registry defaults stop creation, and Phala commands use an isolated working directory so a caller’s local phala.toml cannot change the deployment. This gives operators a clearer, registry-controlled creation path. The manifest is 0.5.22-dev and the latest public release observed was 0.5.21; no mainnet rollout, exploit remediation or independent execution test is claimed.

updates.headline: SN36 Weir commits GPU price floor and model-linked activation fee checks
updates.summary: November 5 Eastern commits accept GPU prices between half the model cap and the full cap; under-floor GPUs are not rented and earn no idle pay. New activations remember the model, with a seven-day deadline to top up if a higher-fee model is reported. Insufficiently covered GPUs are withheld from earnings and rental; expiry resets activation, restoring prior payment as credit. Legacy activations without model records are exempt. Code and upstream tests were reviewed, without running those tests or verifying live rollout.

updates.headline: SN92 REAX 1.3 records 74.0 on the independent Decision Index
updates.summary: On November 6, the public Decision Index 0.4.1 shows SN92 REAX 1.3 at 74.0, ahead numerically of GLiDE 27B at 73.4, while the full-results table marks both at tied rank =1. The Full score combines 60% private same-skill tests and 40% private new-domain tasks; public benchmarks are displayed but do not count. Open model files and a two-part engine are available. The model repository was last modified November 3, so today’s development is the independent result and announcement, not a newly uploaded model. The card’s internal 73.71 measurement is a separate public-suite result. No independent rerun, general intelligence superiority or commercial adoption is claimed. Following the morning announcement, shared node-derived snapshots show alpha/TAO rising from 0.019668351 at 15:00:12 UTC to 0.026876723 at 17:36:12 UTC, a 36.65% increase. That observed market response supports the story’s significance; timing alone does not establish that the news caused the move.
